judged_text: The duplicate check reads booking.attendees (lines 74-78) and then inserts in a separate update with no unique index on Attendee(bookingId, email) — a check-then-insert TOCTOU with nothing backing it at the schema level. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking and the same email both pass the filter and both execute createMany, producing duplicate Attendee rows that no constraint forbids; the same missing invariant also lets any other write path create the same duplicate.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a read (prisma.booking.findFirst include attendees) then filters `uniqueGuests` using `booking.attendees` and later performs a separate `prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`. This is a classic non-atomic check-then-write flow, so concurrent `addGuests` calls could bypass the in-memory duplicate filter and race at insert time. However, the finding’s claim that there is “no unique index on Attendee(bookingId, email)” and that duplicates are therefore definitely insertable is not verifiable from this diff (no Prisma schema/DB constraints shown).
